fullPassage: Play is a fundamental aspect of human development that continues all through our lives. Playgrounds serve as a central place for play, but many individuals struggle to fully engage in these spaces due to their restrictive arrangements. Often, playgrounds are designed to satisfy specific types of play or particular age groups, which can leave children who cannot participate in the intended manner feeling excluded. For children with disabilities, play is even more crucial as it offers an opportunity to practice social skills. However, the conventional design of playgrounds does not typically accommodate their needs, either overwhelming or boring them. A visit to a standard playground with children with disabilities can highlight the weaknesses in design that fail to satisfy everyone. Playgrounds should be designed to foster social connections for all ages, provide sensory stimulation, encourage physical exercise, and connect with nature. Achieving this integration is a challenging design task. By involving children with disabilities and their families in the design process and creating friendlier playgrounds, we can acknowledge that play is more than just a source of enjoyment. This approach results in spaces where people of all abilities, ages, and languages can take part in the joy of play. For example, Martin’s Park, designed by Michael Van Valkenburgh Associates, is a universally designed playground. Unusual play structures and a large ship provide endless experiences of play that can engage every child. The various methods of play have different means of access, allowing kids who are able to scramble up hills, while children who can’t walk can use the sloping paths to reach the top. Interpretive signs point out the inclusive routes and elements of the playground. The inclusion of more than 1,000 trees grants children and adults the chance to experience the sensory aspects of plants. Play isn’t just for kids anymore. Senior play spaces and public exercise equipment are being installed around the world. Play spaces for older adults provide health benefits and encourage engagement with their families and community. Hence, playgrounds need to be redesigned as spaces where everyone can enjoy themselves.
title: Universal Design Playground
